summary: EUR invoice total differs from Console estimate due to exchange-rate rounding and VAT handling
description:
Issue summary:
SkyMap Analytics reports a ~€18.43 difference between the invoice total in the PDF (final invoice for 2026-02) and the estimate shown in the Redwood Console prior to invoice generation. They are a Dedicated customer billed monthly in EUR.

Impact:
Customer is concerned about accuracy of final billing and wants an itemized explanation and corrective action if the discrepancy is caused by metering or incorrect tax application. The difference is small relative to the invoice but they expect exact parity or a clear reconciliation.

Environment / Account details:
- Customer account: org: skymap-analytics (internal id x-98765)
- Billing currency: EUR (customer located in Ireland, VAT applicable)
- Billing model: Dedicated (monthly reserved + burst)
- Invoice number: RWI-2026-02-3187 (attached PDF name: invoice_RWI-2026-02-3187.pdf)
- Console estimate snapshot: estimate_2026-02-28-20z.csv (attached)

Steps to reproduce / what customer did:
1) Viewed cost estimate in Redwood Console on 2026-02-28 for the Feb billing window (exported CSV).
2) Noted total: €1,237.52 (Console estimate, pre-invoice).
3) Received final invoice email on 2026-03-03 with PDF total: €1,255.95.
4) Downloaded invoice PDF and compared line items vs console export; subtotal lines align within cents but final total differs by €18.43.

Expected behavior:
Console estimate and final invoice should match or the invoice should include a clearly labeled reconciliation line (exchange-rate adjustment, tax rounding, or late usage correction).

Actual behavior observed:
Final invoice contains an unlabeled line "Exchange rate adjustment" for €18.43 (negative to customer) visible in PDF but not shown in Console estimate or in the exported CSV. VAT rows appear to be computed on the post-adjustment subtotal in the PDF, while Console shows VAT computed on the pre-adjustment subtotal.

Attachments provided by customer:
- invoice_RWI-2026-02-3187.pdf
- estimate_2026-02-28-20z.csv
- screenshot_console_cost_breakdown.png

Customer's ask:
1) Explain why the exchange-rate adjustment was applied and why it did not appear in the Console estimate export.
2) Confirm whether VAT was calculated correctly and whether the adjustment is tax-inclusive/exclusive.
3) If this is an error in billing pipeline, apply a credit and provide a corrected invoice.

Notes / quick hypotheses for investigation:
- Billing pipeline uses daily FX feed (internal) sourced from ECB close rate; Console estimate uses a cached last-day rate which may differ by a few tenths of a percent.
- Rounding policy differences: Console shows rounded per-line amounts but invoice engine aggregates and applies rounding at invoice-level causing small mismatch.
- Timing: A late-metered burst (post-cutoff) could have been included in final invoice but absent from estimate; customer asserts their usage CSV has no additional lines.
- VAT treatment: Invoice generator may apply VAT after adjustments while Console applies VAT to pre-adjustment subtotal.

Recommended first actions:
- Ask Billing team to confirm FX rate used on invoice date and provide the rate/EUR-USD table for 2026-02-28 -> 2026-03-03.
- Run a reconciliation script comparing Console-exported line-by-line to invoice generator inputs and capture any late usage rows.
- Provide customer with a breakdown PDF showing how the €18.43 was derived (rate, rounding, tax delta).
